transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As we discussed, the company plans to make our clinical documentation platform available to external customers on October 1, and the platform has completed its internal engineering pilot with no unresolved performance blockers. Our current launch packet uses the company's standard software, privacy, product-description, and enterprise-contract templates. Before I give final authorization, I need each of you as functional counsel to state any legal condition that must be included in the launch packet. Let's go around the table.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical license review finding before we proceed. My completed license review of the production build confirmed that module M-17 incorporates an AGPL-licensed library. Under the company's approved proprietary deployment policy, M-17 must be replaced before any external customer access. I have not yet added this result to the launch packet, so this is a legal condition that must be included: the M-17 module must be replaced with a compliant alternative before we can authorize external customer access on October 1.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a privacy condition before we proceed. In the signed design-partner agreement, I confirmed that customer content may not be used to train or improve the company's models and must be deleted within exactly 30 days after account termination. I have not yet updated the standard privacy language in the launch packet to reflect these commitments. This is a legal condition that must be included: the privacy template in the launch packet must be revised to incorporate these binding restrictions on customer content use and the 30-day deletion requirement before we can authorize external customer access on October 1.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag an intended-use condition before we proceed. My intended-use review concluded that the planned language describing automated clinical triage recommendations makes diagnostic claims, which the launch materials must instead describe the product as an administrative workflow tool only. I have not yet circulated that review, so this is a legal condition that must be included: the product-description language in the launch packet must be revised to describe the platform as an administrative workflow tool only, with no diagnostic claims regarding automated clinical triage recommendations, before we can authorize external customer access on October 1.
